title: Decode a caption, then prove its claims
description: Compare search strategies on one finite candidate set. Decoder confidence ranks wording; six separate evidence records decide which claims can be released.
evidenceNote: All candidates, confidence values, probability masses, and region scores are hand-authored synthetic evidence for this lab. They are not measured model performance or benchmark results.

scene.label: Synthetic street scene
scene.summary: One person rides a bicycle on a city street. A red jacket is visible; the helmet is partly occluded. No dog is present in the labeled scene.

evidence.label: bicycle
evidence.detail: Frame and two wheels are visible.

evidence.label: city street
evidence.detail: Road, curb, and buildings support the setting.

evidence.label: red jacket
evidence.detail: The rider's outer garment is visibly red.

evidence.label: helmet
evidence.detail: The head area is partly occluded, so the object is uncertain.

evidence.label: dog
evidence.detail: A low-confidence proposal conflicts with the labeled scene.

constraints.label: No lexical constraint
constraints.detail: Let the selected decoding strategy choose among every candidate.

constraints.label: Require “helmet”
constraints.detail: Force a terminology requirement even though helmet evidence is uncertain.

constraints.label: Require “dog”
constraints.detail: Demonstrate how a lexical rule can force an unsupported object.

candidates.caption: A person rides a bicycle on a city street.
A person in a red jacket rides a bicycle on a city street.
A helmeted cyclist rides a bicycle on a city street.
A cyclist rides a bicycle past a dog.
